provenance.authorship: Original project scenario, AI-assisted draft. Practitioner review and scoring calibration pending.

title: Engineering Manager: Improve On-Call Without Blaming the Responder
prompt: Review a draft incident follow-up: "The responder took 25 minutes to find the right runbook. Action: remind engineers to be more careful. Increase on-call shifts until response time improves." There were six noisy alerts before the actionable one; the runbook link pointed to an archived page. The team has five engineers and no additional on-call budget this month. Propose a management response and an accountable follow-up.

rubric.label: Distinguish system and individual evidence
rubric.description: Uses the timeline without assigning unsupported blame.

anchors.0: Concludes carelessness from response time or treats all pages as unavoidable.
anchors.2: Identifies the broken runbook and alert noise.
anchors.4: Reconstructs the response and escalation, separates observed actions from assumptions and identifies missing ownership and overlapping demands as testable contributors.

rubric.label: Choose bounded corrective work
rubric.description: Links changes to the documented problem.

anchors.0: Adds shifts or disables alerts without checking consequences.
anchors.2: Assigns owners to runbooks and alert review.
anchors.4: Sets a small service-owner-reviewed alert change and verified runbook repair, with completion evidence, balancing checks and a rollback/escalation plan if coverage degrades.

rubric.label: Manage capacity and learning
rubric.description: Makes reliability work feasible and learning safe.

anchors.0: Requires indefinite extra on-call work as punishment.
anchors.2: Accounts for the current staffing and workload.
anchors.4: Reprioritizes funded capacity with stakeholders, checks responder support and follow-up burden, and reviews recurrence and actionable-page load rather than using response speed alone.

reference.scenario: Review a draft incident follow-up: "The responder took 25 minutes to find the right runbook. Action: remind engineers to be more careful. Increase on-call shifts until response time improves." There were six noisy alerts before the actionable one; the runbook link pointed to an archived page. The team has five engineers and no additional on-call budget this month. Propose a management response and an accountable follow-up.

facts.value: The responder escalated after ten minutes. The backup was handling another alert. No single owner is assigned to runbook links or alert usefulness.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about the timeline, escalation or ownership

facts.value: Two low-value alerts account for half of overnight pages. Changing them requires service-owner review and a check that important signals remain covered.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about a bounded improvement or alert quality

model_points: Reconstructs the response and escalation, separates observed actions from assumptions and identifies missing ownership and overlapping demands as testable contributors.
Sets a small service-owner-reviewed alert change and verified runbook repair, with completion evidence, balancing checks and a rollback/escalation plan if coverage degrades.
Reprioritizes funded capacity with stakeholders, checks responder support and follow-up burden, and reviews recurrence and actionable-page load rather than using response speed alone.

probes.question: Which supplied failure would still exist after everyone repeats training?
How will you verify that important failures remain detectable?

probes.trigger: candidate revises an initial blame statement
probes.question: How would you correct that statement in the incident record?

fair_alternatives: Additional training is valid if it addresses demonstrated knowledge gaps alongside the broken system.
A different small alert pilot is acceptable with a coverage check and owner.
reference.assessment_limits: Assess only the decisions and reasoning demonstrated in this fictional exercise. No hiring-readiness, personality, legal compliance or workplace performance claim follows from this score. A valid alternative can earn full credit. Unrevealed conditional facts must not be assumed known or required for credit; credit asking for needed information and a conditional plan.

interviewer_notes: You are the counterpart named in the prompt. If this is a written review, remain the hiring interviewer while the candidate reads and writes. Let the candidate finish, including thinking and self-correction. Answer only supplied facts when their reveal condition is met; otherwise say the information is unknown. Use neutral probes after a completed answer, one at a time. Do not prescribe the rubric as a spoken checklist. Accept relevant examples from work, education and community leadership. Do not request private employee records, infer protected traits, invent employment rules or promise a real organizational outcome. Simulation gives no answer before assessment; coaching may offer labeled assistance.

learning_drills.title: Rewrite an incident action
learning_drills.prompt: Replace the draft reminder with two owned, verifiable improvements and a balancing measure. This is self-guided practice with no automated assessment.
